polityNote: Oblasts of Ukraine from the Act of Declaration of Independence (24 Aug 1991) to the dissolution of the USSR; the present-day units are carried back from 26 Dec 1991 and OpenHistoricalMap’s Ukrainian SSR ends 16 Sep 1991, leaving the autumn of 1991 unanswered. Atoms: geoBoundaries UKR ADM1 (OpenStreetMap/Wambacher 2017, ODbL, 137,991 vertices vs. 19,652 in Natural Earth). Check ① (2026-10-06, 0.05° grid) against the OpenHistoricalMap oblasts in force on 1991-10-01: IoU 0.97–1.00 for Sumy, Chernihiv, Kharkiv, Donetsk, Mykolaiv, Luhansk, Zakarpattia; Zaporizhzhia 0.90 and Kherson 0.84, where the OpenStreetMap atoms extend over the Sea of Azov / Dnieper reservoir water that OHM leaves out (OHM is ≥0.98 inside the atoms).

sources.title: Statoids — Regions of Ukraine, change history
sources.says: The last boundary changes listed are Cherkasy (about 1955) and Drohobych into Lviv (about 1963); from 1991 only names and the status of Crimea (1992) change.

sources.title: Wikipedia — Oblasts of Ukraine
sources.says: Ukraine has had 24 oblasts since 1991 (with the Autonomous Republic of Crimea and the cities of Kyiv and Sevastopol); the Crimean Oblast (1954–1991) became the Crimean ASSR.

Kyiv city limits after 1991 are not established from a change list.
